Reading: Read a range of narrative and informational texts and identify overall meaning and key details.

Infer characters' feelings and reasons for actions when reading.
Compare information from two short texts on a familiar topic.
Writing: Write a clear paragraph with a topic sentence and supporting details.
Use conjunctions and sequencers to connect ideas with developing coherence.
Write for different purposes (recount, description, instructions).
Revise and edit writing for spelling, capitals and punctuation.
Vocabulary: Topic vocabulary for community, journeys and daily life
Academic verbs: describe, compare, explain, suggest
Time and sequence words: first, next, finally, meanwhile

Listening: ENG.03.L.S.3.1 — Take simple notes with increasing accuracy when listening to simple texts on familiar and concrete topics that use simple language and are spoken slowly and clearly, and when prompts and clarification are provided.

ENG.03.S.IP.2.1 — Ask and answer questions on familiar and concrete topics in short and simple interactions, seeking clarification when needed and giving short responses to open- ended questions using an increasing range of familiar phrases and expressions, although there may be frequent pauses.

ENG.03.L.CS.4.1 — Infer the meaning of unknown words and expressions from the context when listening to simple texts on familiar and concrete topics that use simple language and are spoken slowly and clearly.

ENG.03.S.IP.5.1 — Deliver short, prepared presentations on familiar and concrete topics where ideas are connected with the use of a range of basic cohesive devices, answering a limited range of simple follow-up questions, although there may be frequent pauses.
ENG.03.L.CS.5.1 — Listen and identify some details in simple texts on familiar and concrete topics that use simple language and are spoken slowly and clearly.

ENG.03.S.IP.6.1 — Summarise and describe the main points and information in simple written, spoken or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics, using an increasing range of familiar phrases and expressions when speaking, although there may be frequent pauses.
ENG.03.L.PA.4.1 — Identify a wide range of intonation patterns when listening to simple texts on familiar and concrete topics that use simple language and are spoken slowly and clearly.
ENG.03.S.P.2.1 — Produce connected speech with correct stress, intonation and rhythm, though occasional errors may still occur.
Speaking: ENG.03.S.IP.1.1 — Participate in short, simple conversations on familiar and concrete topics using an increasing range of familiar phrases and expressions, although there may be frequent pauses.
ENG.03.L.CS.1.1 — Listen and identify the overall meaning of simple texts on familiar and concrete topics that use simple language and are spoken slowly and clearly.

ENG.03.S.IP.2.1 — Ask and answer questions on familiar and concrete topics in short and simple interactions, seeking clarification when needed and giving short responses to open- ended questions using an increasing range of familiar phrases and expressions, although there may be frequent pauses.

ENG.03.RV.S.3.3 — Apply an increasing range of reading strategies, including, using context, first language, culture, experiences, developing oral language skills, text format and appearance, known words, and rereading and reading on to understand and interpret simple written or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics that are clearly structured and use simple language.

ENG.03.S.F.2.1 — Produce simple spoken texts on familiar and concrete topics, expressing simple comparisons and justifications where appropriate in a simple list of points and linked sentences with an increasing ability to convey meaning, often using self-correction and repetition, although there may be frequent pauses.

ENG.03.RV.CS.3.1 — Make simple connections between ideas, events, characters or themes and own experience, background knowledge, other familiar texts or the world around them to support understanding of new texts when reading simple written or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics that are clearly structured and use simple language.

ENG.03.S.IP.5.1 — Deliver short, prepared presentations on familiar and concrete topics where ideas are connected with the use of a range of basic cohesive devices, answering a limited range of simple follow-up questions, although there may be frequent pauses.
ENG.03.RV.CS.6.1 — Read and identify the main points of simple written or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics that are clearly structured and use simple language.
Language Focus: ENG.03.S.IP.4.1 — Express simple ideas, information, opinions, feelings and emotions on familiar and concrete topics using an increasing range of familiar phrases and expressions in simple spoken texts with developing coherence, although there may be frequent pauses.

ENG.03.WR.P.2.1 — Express simple ideas, information, opinions, feelings and emotions on familiar and concrete topics using an increasing range of familiar phrases and expressions in simple written or multimodal texts with developing coherence, although there may be inaccuracies and repetition of vocabulary and structures.

ENG.03.WR.P.2.1 — Express simple ideas, information, opinions, feelings and emotions on familiar and concrete topics using an increasing range of familiar phrases and expressions in simple written or multimodal texts with developing coherence, although there may be inaccuracies and repetition of vocabulary and structures.
ENG.03.S.F.3.1 — Use a range of basic cohesive devices to connect ideas in simple spoken texts on familiar and concrete topics with developing coherence, although there may be frequent pauses.

ENG.03.S.F.1.1 — Engage in short, simple exchanges on familiar and concrete topics using linked sentences with an increasing ability to convey meaning, often using self-correction and repetition, although there may be frequent pauses.

ENG.03.WR.S.5.1 — Use a range of basic cohesive devices to connect ideas in simple written or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics with developing coherence, although there may be inaccuracies and repetition of vocabulary and structures.

ENG.03.S.IP.7.1 — Interpret and describe simple visuals on familiar and concrete topics using an increasing range of familiar phrases and expressions when speaking, although there may be frequent pauses.
ENG.03.WR.S.3.1 — Write sentences using a wide range of punctuation with a high level of control.
Reading and Viewing: ENG.03.RV.CS.2.1 — Read and identify specific information in simple written or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics that are clearly structured and use simple language.

Reading: Use simple reading strategies such as using context, known words, rereading and text layout to understand short, familiar written or multimodal texts that are clearly organised and easy to follow.
Connect ideas, events, characters or themes from simple reading texts to personal experiences, background knowledge or other familiar texts to help understand new topics.
Connect what they read to their own experiences, background knowledge, other texts, and the world around them to help them understand simple, familiar texts.
Find and write down key information from one or two simple texts on familiar topics, showing that you can tell the difference between facts and opinions.
Read and find specific information in short, simple written or multimodal texts about familiar topics that are clearly organised and use basic language.
Read and understand the main idea of short, simple written or multimodal texts about familiar topics that are clearly organised and use basic language.
Writing: Summarise and describe the main ideas from simple written, spoken or multimodal texts on familiar topics, using common phrases and expressions in writing, even with some mistakes or repetition.
Use simple planning and revising strategies, such as graphic organisers, text models or templates, to write and improve short texts on familiar topics, even with some errors or repetition.
Use strategies like graphic organizers, sample texts, and templates to help students write and revise simple texts on familiar topics, even if there are some mistakes or repeated words.
Write short, simple texts about familiar topics, expressing ideas, opinions and feelings using clear sentences and common phrases, even with some errors or repetition.
Use simple linking words to connect ideas in short pieces of writing on familiar topics, showing growing control, even if some mistakes or repetition occur.
Write about past stories, experiences or events with key details, using familiar words and phrases in simple texts, even with some mistakes or repetition.

Language Focus: ENG.04.WR.P.1.1 — Produce simple and some extended written or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics, expressing comparisons and justifications where appropriate with an increasing ability to convey meaning, although there may be some inaccuracies and repetition of vocabulary and structures.
ENG.04.RV.CS.1.1 — Read and identify the overall meaning of simple, extended written or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics that are clearly expressed and structured.

ENG.04.S.IP.6.1 — Summarise and describe the main points and information in simple written, spoken or multimodal texts on familiar and concrete topics using a wide range of phrases and expressions when speaking, although there may be some pauses.

Reading: "Apply a wide range of reading strategies, including: - using context - using first language - using culture and experiences - using developing oral language skills - using text format and appearance - using the main message and known…

Make logical connections between ideas, events, characters or themes and own experience, background knowledge, other familiar texts or the world around them and give simple reasons for these connections when reading.
Make basic inferences or predictions about text content, line of argumentation and sequence of events in a narrative, using text features and basic connectors when reading.
Identify key features of text, including, format, appearance, organisation and structure, in a wide range of text types when reading.
Select and group relevant information to support a topic or question when reading two or more texts.
Read and identify specific information. Lesson 12 PPT Writing and Representing p114-115
Writing: "Apply a wide range of pre- and post-writing strategies, including: - graphic organisers - writing plans - models - shared writing - brainstorming - conferencing - language knowledge to produce and revise texts with emerging…

Make logical connections between ideas, events, characters or themes and own experience, background knowledge, other familiar texts or the world around them and give simple reasons for these connections when reading.
Recount detailed stories, past experiences and events that are sequenced, expressing feelings and reasons for those feelings in response to the event or experience in writing.
Use a range of basic cohesive devices, and some referencing or substitution to connect ideas in written or multimodal texts with developing coherence.
Produce simple and some extended written or multimodal texts, expressing comparisons and justifications where appropriate.
Spell many challenging words with accuracy. Lesson 20 PPT Speaking p132-133

Reading: Extract and organise relevant information to support clear claims when reading multiple texts, considering the reliability of information and distinguishing between evidence and opin Lesson 23 PPT Reading and Writing p77-80 Connectors…

Read and identify the overall meaning. Lesson 11 PPT Reading and Writing p56- 60 Modals of certainty (should, must, can); linking words (because, however, so) How To Develop My Students' Reading Skills metabolism, calories, regain…
Make inferences or predictions about text content, line of argumentation, and the meaning of sections of text, using whole text comprehension, and text features and organisation when reading.
Apply a wide range of reading strategies, including: using context, using first language, using culture and experiences and using the main message to understand and interpret texts.
Infer the meaning of unknown words and expressions from the context and knowledge of word parts (prefixes, suffixes, etc.) when reading.
Writing: Recount detailed stories, past experiences and events that are clearly sequenced, and clearly express feelings and reasons for those feelings in response to the event or experience in writing.
Collate and summarise short pieces of information from different text sources in writing Lesson 24 PPT Reading and Writing p77-80 Past simple / past continuous
Express ideas, information, opinions, feelings, emotions and personal perspectives, giving simple reasons and explanations in writing.
Interpret and describe the overall trends, main points and detailed information in visuals and diagrams in writing.
Summarise and paraphrase information and arguments in texts, giving details where needed in writing.

Unit 1: Introduction to health: HSC1.1.01.001 — Explain the concept of health and illness.
HSC1.1.01.002 — Identify the dimensions of health (physical, social, mental and emotional).
HSC1.1.01.003 — Describe the factors that contribute to physical health.
HSC1.1.01.004 — Describe the factors that contribute to social health.
HSC1.1.01.005 — Describe the factors that contribute to mental health.
HSC1.1.01.006 — Describe the factors that contribute to emotional health.
HSC1.1.01.007 — Define the stages of human growth and development.
Unit 2: First Aid: HSC.3.1.01.001 — Explain the purpose of first aid and identify who can provide it.
HSC.3.1.01.002 — List the contents of a first aid kit.
HSC.3.1.01.003 — Demonstrate the initial steps to take at the scene of an emergency.
HSC.3.1.01.004 — Apply the principles of hygiene and infection control to first aid.
HSC.3.1.01.005 — Differentiate between arterial, venous and capillary bleeding.
HSC.3.1.01.006 — Identify different types of open soft tissue injuries.
Unit 3: Anatomy and physiology: HSC5.1.01.001 — Explain the concept of homeostasis.
HSC5.1.01.002 — Describe the different types of tissues and their function.
HSC5.1.01.003 — Describe the structure and function of the musculoskeletal system.
HSC5.1.01.005 — Describe the structure and function of the circulatory system.
HSC5.1.01.006 — Describe the structure and function of the respiratory system.
HSC5.1.01.007 — Describe the structure and function of the nervous system.
HSC5.1.01.008 — Describe the structure and function of the digestive system.
HSC5.1.01.009 — Describe the components and function of the immune system.
Unit 4: Healthcare and ethics: HSC3.2.01.002 — List the types of healthcare professionals and their roles.
HSC3.2.01.001 — Identify different health services available in the community.
HSC3.2.01.007 — Compare and contrast inpatient and outpatient care.
HSC3.2.01.003 — Explain patient’s rights and responsibilities in healthcare.
HSC3.2.01.008 — Define ethics in relation to healthcare.
HSC3.2.01.005 — Identify the legal and ethical regulations that apply to healthcare.
HSC3.2.01.009 — Explain the moral basis of patient confidentiality.
HSC3.2.01.006 — Identify the major principles of patient safety and harm prevention.

Reading: Interpret and evaluate relevant information to support a topic, question or claim when reading multiple texts, considering the reliability and credibility of sources, and identifying differences in perspectives or reasoning.
Make inferences or predictions about text content, line of argumentation, and the meaning of sections of text, using whole text comprehension, and text features and organisation when reading.
Apply a wide range of reading strategies, including: using context, using culture and experiences, and using the main message to understand and interpret texts.
Infer the meaning of unknown words and expressions from the context and knowledge of word parts (prefixes, suffixes, etc.) when reading.
Take accurate, organised notes in own words, with precision and appropriate detail when reading.
Read and identify specific information. Lesson 11 PPT Reading and Writing p59- 60
Writing: Produce written or multimodal texts that generally follow conventional text-type features appropriate to the task, contain paragraphs with topic sentences and supporting details, and show a developing awareness of audience.
Recount detailed stories, past experiences and events that are clearly sequenced, and clearly express feelings and reasons for those feelings in response to the event or experience in writing.
Use an increasing range of cohesive devices, and referencing or substitution to connect ideas in written or multimodal texts that are generally coherent.
Express ideas, information, opinions, feelings, emotions and personal perspectives, giving reasons and explanations in writing.
Interpret and describe the overall trends, main points and detailed information in visuals, diagrams and charts in writing.
Apply a wide range of pre- and post- writing strategies, including writing plans to produce and revise texts independently.

Reading: Interpret and analyse explicit and implicit connections between ideas, perspectives or themes and own experience, background knowledge, other texts or the wider world to support conclusions when reading.
Apply a wide range of reading strategies, including: - using context - using culture and experiences - adjusting reading rate - scanning to understand, interpret and analyse texts.
Identify, interpret and analyse conventional features of text, including, format, appearance, organisation, structure and language, in a wide range of text types when reading.
Infer meaning and make predictions using a variety of strategies, including using contextual clues, whole text knowledge, text features and organisation, etc. when reading.
Analyse and evaluate relevant information to support claims when reading multiple texts, determining credibility, reliability, relevance and sufficiency of evidence.
Read and identify details in extended written or multimodal texts on concrete and some abstract topics that may use some nonstandard language.
Writing: Produce structured written or multimodal texts that follow conventional text-type features appropriate to the task, contain paragraphs with topic sentences and supporting details, and show an increasing awareness of audience.

Apply a wide range of pre- and post-writing strategies, including: - model analysis - rubrics - drafting and redrafting - language knowledge to produce and revise texts extensively and independently when given time.
Recount clear, detailed stories, past experiences and events that are clearly sequenced, and clearly express feelings and reasons for those feelings in response to the event or experience in writing.
Express ideas, information, opinions, feelings, emotions and personal perspectives, giving detailed reasons and explanations at some length when speaking.
Use a wide range of cohesive devices, and referencing or substitution to connect ideas in written or multimodal texts, ensuring coherence throughout.
Interpret and describe reliably the overall trends, main points and detailed information in complex visuals, diagrams and charts in writing.

__science_framework.source: Science C3 CCG Unified Lesson Plan Template (2026-27)
scientificMethod: Gather background information and do research
Plan the experiment (design the investigation and identify variables)
Reflect and propose next steps or further investigations
__science_framework.assessmentRules: Cycle 3 science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology): Performance tasks are 40% of the term’s continuous-assessment score — at least one performance task and one lab per module, varied task types across modules. Dedicate 60–80% of assessment to Power outcomes and 20–40% to Support outcomes (Basic and Supplementary).
__science_framework.threeDimensional: Three-dimensional learning: questions should combine a science & engineering practice, a disciplinary core idea and a crosscutting concept, and preferably explain a phenomenon or solve a problem (Performance Expectation style).

rules: Assess across Bloom’s levels: remember/understand (MCQ, matching, labelling diagrams, short answer, sorting), apply (practical/lab-based or paper-based scenarios), analyse/evaluate (explanations, comparing, judging claims), create (design or research-style tasks).
Balance selected-response items (recall of concepts and simple procedures) with constructed-response items (explain, show working, demonstrate deeper understanding).
Quizzes and tasks should match the rigour and challenge of the end-of-term exams for the grade.
Diagnostic tests (Term 1, weeks 2–3): sections at increasing difficulty, 2–3 questions per key outcome, about 20–30 questions, including prerequisite outcomes from earlier grades.
Diagnostic tiers by score: Tier 1 80–100 (ready to be challenged), Tier 2 45–79 (needs some support), Tier 3 0–44 (needs prerequisite skills).

School-based Summative Assessment (Grades 9–12, Term 2): exam-style, focused on Term 2 outcomes, a variety of question types across difficulty levels and Bloom’s levels so results spread normally; keep papers, mark schemes and specification tables.
